Welcome to my classroom!
Ask me anything about building a green town, and I’ll show you on the big screen.
Or pick a mission to test my plans.
I learn from patterns, not from looking at the real island.
So I can sound very sure and still be wrong!
That’s why you check my plans with a lens before you build.
Pick a lens: it shows what my plan would really do, like flooding or carbon.
If the lens shows a problem, I made a mistake, and you caught it!

Town land: Marks land where your town can grow.
Homes, shops and the hall go here.
Keep wild: A promise to leave this land wild for plants and animals.
Car road: Lets cars get around, but cars are noisy, dirty and less safe to cross.
Car park: Space to leave cars.
Handy, but it makes more car trips.
Footpath & crossing: A safe way to walk, with a crossing over busy roads.
Cycle lane: A lane for bikes: quick, quiet and healthy.
Tram stop: A tram takes lots of people across town without cars.
Bridge: Lets people cross the river.
Timber terrace: Wooden homes for 4 families.
Wood makes little carbon to build with, and keeps homes warm.
Straw-bale cottages: Cosy straw-bale cottages for 3 families.
Straw keeps homes very warm.
Rammed-earth homes: Thick earth walls for 3 families.
They stay cool in summer and warm in winter.
Reclaimed-brick terrace: Homes for 4 families built from old bricks, so less new stuff is made.
Cohousing court: Homes for 5 families around a shared garden.
Neighbours help each other.
Concrete flats: Flats for 6 families, but concrete makes a lot of carbon and they get cold.
Green roof: Plants on a roof: homes for bees and birds, and less rain runs off.
Big field: One huge field makes lots of food, but leaves no room for wildlife.
Mixed farm: A farm with animals and crops together.
Good food, kind to the land.
Orchard: Fruit trees: food for people and flowers for bees.
Allotments: Little gardens where neighbours grow vegetables together.
Vertical farm: Food grown indoors on shelves.
Lots of food, but it needs electricity.
Beehives: Bees pollinate orchards and allotments, so they grow more food.
Plant a hedge: A hedge is a home and a safe path for wildlife.
Solar roof: Panels on a roof make electricity from sunshine (but not on winter nights).
Heat pump: Warms a home with electricity instead of burning gas.
Wind turbine: Makes clean electricity whenever the wind blows, even on winter nights.
Battery store: Saves spare electricity for later, like on a still winter night.
Rain garden: Soaks up rainwater so streets don’t flood.
Reed bed: Reeds clean dirty water naturally and give wildlife a home.
Repair café: People fix old things here instead of throwing them away.
Compost hub: Turns food scraps into soil for the farms.
Market square: A square where people meet and sell local food.
Park: Green space to play and relax, for people and wildlife.
Green bridge: A bridge covered in plants so animals can cross safely too.
Community hall: A hall for clubs, parties and town meetings.
Festival field: A field for fairs and festivals that bring everyone together.
